verdicts.reason: Quote states active-low reset, async assert, sync release; scenario check fine.

Quote only says o_tx_ready means transmitter can accept a byte at next edge; handshake acceptance is a stream rule. Actor should be the transmitter slave, ok, but checkable from interface only partially (acceptance not visible). Scenario is right; keep the scenario check but the strength is a meaning statement, so SHOULD is not warranted. Keep MUST with scenario.
Reset value 1 stated; checkable after reset.
Bit 0 sent first is stated, but the transmitter on o_txd is the actor (slave of the tx stream), not source.

Meaning states o_rx_valid indicates holding register holds a byte; holding register is internal, so not checkable from interface; scenario is right. Actor is the receiver driving the stream (master/source).
The consumer taking the byte at the i_rx_ready edge is a handshake; actor is the receiver driving o_rx_valid, which is the source.
Reset value 0 stated; actor should be the source of the rx stream.
Data content and bit order are stated; actor is the source of the rx stream.
Reset value 0 stated; actor should be source.
Stated by quote; the stop bit sampling is internal so scenario check; actor is source.
Reset value 0 stated; actor should be source.
One-cycle pulse is stated; actor is source; check should be scenario since the drop condition depends on internal state and needs stimulus.

Reset value 1 and idle high are stated; actor is the transmitter (slave) of the tx stream, and idle-high is checkable only with knowledge of idle, so use scenario for idle; reset value is assertion. Use both.

Quote says the line is synchronised inside the block, an internal implementation detail; the input is driven by the environment, so the actor is the system and it is not directly verifiable at the interface. Keep as scenario with asynchronous stimulus.

questions.question: Is o_rx_valid/o_rx_data/o_rx_frame_err reset-value assertion meaningful when the reset is asserted asynchronously, and does reset clear them immediately?
Are the master/slave/source/destination roles for the tx and rx streams defined (which side drives valid and which drives ready)?
Does o_rx_frame_err hold its value while o_rx_valid is low, or is it don't-care?
